query: What product attributes are associated with higher satisfaction scores?

per_column.name: mentioned_attributes
per_column.rationale: Interpretable product-attribute categories that can be segmented against satisfaction; directly serves the query about which attributes associate with higher scores. Slightly fine-grained due to multi-label combinations, but individual labels are meaningful.

per_column.name: attribute_count
per_column.rationale: Small discrete count (0-9) giving a clean ordinal scale to compare satisfaction across breadth of attributes mentioned; interpretable and groupable.

per_column.name: attr_taste_flavor
per_column.rationale: Clear binary present/absent split with well-balanced classes; ideal for grouped comparison of satisfaction by whether taste is discussed.

per_column.name: attr_texture
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary attribute flag; classes reasonably populated (1657 positives) for meaningful segmentation.

per_column.name: attr_smell_aroma
per_column.rationale: Binary flag; somewhat imbalanced (470 positives) but still a distinct, interpretable segment for comparison.

per_column.name: attr_quality
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary attribute; well-populated classes support satisfaction comparison.

per_column.name: attr_packaging
per_column.rationale: Balanced binary flag directly relevant to product-attribute association with satisfaction.

per_column.name: attr_value_price
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary, well-populated; price mentions can be compared against satisfaction.

per_column.name: attr_ingredients
per_column.rationale: Clear binary attribute segment relevant to the query.

per_column.name: attr_health_nutrition
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary flag with adequate class sizes for grouped comparison.

per_column.name: attr_size_quantity
per_column.rationale: Balanced binary attribute flag suitable for segmentation against satisfaction.

per_column.name: attr_shipping_delivery
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary; distinguishes fulfillment-related mentions, a meaningful non-product axis to compare.

per_column.name: positive_word_count
per_column.rationale: Positive word count is essentially a proxy for the satisfaction/sentiment being studied; it restates the focus rather than offering an external explanatory attribute.

per_column.name: negative_word_count
per_column.rationale: Negative word count is a near-direct restatement of low satisfaction; also heavily near-constant (0 for 8291 rows), limiting comparison.

per_column.name: sentiment_ratio
per_column.rationale: Derived sentiment measure that is effectively a rephrasing of satisfaction; circular for explaining satisfaction and fine-grained/opaque as a scale.

per_column.name: review_length_bucket
per_column.rationale: Short/medium/long is a clean, interpretable segmentation; a plausible associational (non-restating) axis to compare against satisfaction.

judge.rationale: The bulk of the added columns are exactly what EDA of product-attribute/satisfaction associations needs: a set of interpretable binary attribute flags plus a category label and a count, all groupable with well-separated, adequately populated classes. review_length_bucket adds a clean external axis. The three sentiment-derived columns (positive_word_count, negative_word_count, sentiment_ratio) restate the satisfaction/sentiment focus rather than opening external relationships, and negative_word_count is additionally near-constant. These weaken but do not dominate the set, so the columns as a whole strongly support discovering interpretable relationships with the focus.
